context.situation: I direct operations for a national income-support scheme. We are under a firm instruction to recover historic overpayments. Manual case review is slow and expensive. A proposal would calculate overpayment automatically by averaging annual income data across the year and comparing it to what was paid fortnightly, then issue recovery notices with the burden on the claimant to disprove the figure. Legal have flagged that averaging is an assumption rather than a measurement. The projected recovery is very large, the operational saving is immediate, and the programme is popular with ministers. Claimants can dispute through the existing channel.
context.whatMatters: Meeting the recovery target within budget.
context.stakeholders: Ministers, the agency, claimants, the treasury.
context.uncertainties: Whether averaging produces accurate individual figures.

evidence.text: Averaging annual income is an assumption, not a measurement of fortnightly entitlement.
Legal have flagged the averaging method as an assumption.
Manual review is slow and expensive.
Burden of disproof would sit with the claimant.
An existing dispute channel is available to claimants.
Recipients of this payment are by definition on low or irregular incomes.
Projected recovery is very large and the saving is immediate.
